structure_source: astro-templates/owl/ (role: primary) — fixed section order: hero -> promise-bar -> services-grid -> testimonials -> promise-band -> signature-system -> process-steps -> about -> seo-body -> faq -> blog-cards -> closing-cta -> footer. Native EstimateForm lead capture (posts to /api/estimate), which is why owl is used on this unattended queue build — no operator is present to paste a GHL form snippet.
brand_source: intake-scraped.json → brand.fonts / brand.colors are both null. The client's live site (masonryplus.net) is a legacy GoDaddy Website Builder page whose only color signal is ad-hoc inline WYSIWYG text colors (#FF0000, #A52A2A, #00FFFF) and a font library of dozens of preloaded Google Fonts, neither of which reads as an intentional brand system — see intake-scraped.json _notes.warnings. agcconcrete.com (the vertical's secondary reference) was not re-scraped for this run: its direction is 'earth-tone palette, real photography', which the owl template's own shipped default already matches, so with no client override signal the template default is adopted verbatim rather than inventing a palette with no source to trace it to.

palette._notes: Template shipped default, unmodified — already contrast-verified in astro-templates/owl/src/styles/tokens.css and its README (accent_ink 4.91:1/5.35:1 on bg/surface, accent_on_dark 5.03:1 on primary, on_primary 8.06:1+ on primary). Warm stone/olive/gold reads as a natural fit for a masonry & concrete trade with no conflicting client brand to override it.

typography._notes: Template default — no client font signal to override it with (see brand_source).

avoid: generic construction stock photo (handshake, diverse team in hardhats)
Lucide icon rows (max 1 outline icon per section, semantic only)
"Trusted by 10,000+ customers" without a real number from GBP (use the real 4.9 / 31 reviews instead)
randomized section order — always use the fixed owl order from the template
absolutely-positioned pixel layout / non-responsive design (client-specific: the exact failure mode of the site being replaced, see audit_results.json)
decorative cursive/script webfonts (client-specific: the mismatched font-library noise on the site being replaced)
